Corporate earnings growth is set to slow:

10 of the 11 sectors in the S&P 500 are estimated to record lower YoY earnings growth in Q3 2026, compared to Q2.

We are set for an eventful earnings season.

BREAKING: China’s trade surplus jumped +$67 billion YoY in the first 9 months of 2026, or +7.7%, to a record $938 billion.

This marks its 3rd consecutive YoY increase for this period of the year, totalling +$318 billion.

In September alone, China's trade surplus rose +$50 billion YoY, or +51%, to $134 billion, its 2nd-largest on record.

Exports soared +36% YoY and imports jumped +31%.

At the same time, high-tech shipments surged +64% YoY, accounting for ~50% of total export growth, as global AI infrastructure demand boosted hardware exports.

China’s trade surplus is now on track to exceed the $1.2 trillion record set in 2025.

China is expanding global trade at an unprecedented pace.

BREAKING: Average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving are up +31% YoY, to $402, the highest in at least 10 years.

This marks the 3rd consecutive annual increase, totaling +$133, or +49%.

Since the 2020 pandemic, average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving travel have more than doubled.

By comparison, average round-trip airfares for Christmas are up +23% YoY.

This comes as jet fuel prices have risen +91% since the Iran War began, to ~$4.50 per gallon, driving up airlines’ operating costs.

Americans are facing their priciest holiday travel season in years.

tweets.text:
Ben Horowitz on treating your story as your strategy, and why founders often skip writing it even though it's one of the most important parts of the job:

"The story of the company is also the strategy of the company... In your mind, you're kind of adjusting that strategy a little bit at a time every day. But then a quarter later, it's actually pretty different than what you started with."

"So it's really important that you keep upgrading your story. The articulation of your story. I would definitely recommend it be in written form."

"Something that you can share with everybody in the company, and everybody you're recruiting, everybody you're trying to raise money from, all your constituents, every customer."

"The problem that I think founders have is it doesn't feel like work. Like, 'What are you doing today?' 'I'm working on my story.' That doesn't sound like work."

"Because it doesn't feel like work, people don't do it, but it's probably one of the most important parts of the job."

@bhorowitz w/ @speedrun GP @Tocelot

BREAKING: US margin debt jumped +$26 billion in September, to $1.48 trillion, the 2nd-highest level on record.

Since the start of 2026, margin debt has surged +$255 billion, or +21%.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 4.5%, surpassing the previous peak of 3.6% set in 2021.

At the same time, the margin debt-to-M2 money supply ratio is up to 6.3%, the 3rd-highest level on record.

By comparison, this ratio peaked at 6.4% during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.

Leveraged investing has never been more popular.

Steven Sinofsky on why it's so hard to diffuse AI into companies: most work runs on know-how that's hard to turn into step-by-step instructions for an agent.

"Algorithmic thinking is really, really, really hard for the vast majority of people who have jobs."

"If you were to go to any person and ask them to create a flow chart for a particular thing that they have to go do, they would probably fail at producing that flow chart."

"Say doing a marketing plan and there's 50 marketing people working on a giant product line. One person probably understands and could document the flow chart."

"So if you put one of these agents in front of people to create these things, their ability to explain to it what to do is really, really limited."

"You're basically just developing the next abstraction layer for how people interact. And developing an abstraction layer has historically, at each level of the abstraction layer, been a highly skilled, very specific individual within an organization."

@stevesi

🇩🇪 Germany has lost nearly 500,000 industrial jobs since 2019 according to an Ifo ​study. Yet the country continues to create jobs and that is where the real problem with the German economy lies.

📊 Including certain estimates for temporary workers, the losses could reach 628,000 jobs but all these losses are concentrated in the sectors that have historically driven Germany's industrial strength. We are talking about 123,500 jobs lost in the automotive industry and its suppliers, 115,600 in fabricated metal products, and 64,500 in machinery manufacturing. Together, these three sectors account for 60% of all industrial job losses.

⚠️ Over the same period, the country added approximately 1.7 million jobs overall, largely driven by the services sector, which gained more than 2.2 million jobs. However, a significant share of this job creation has been concentrated in public administration, healthcare, education, and social services. These activities are essential but they do not offer the same potential for productivity gains, innovation, and exports as Germany's traditional industrial sectors.

➡️ To understand this transformation, we need to look at the foundations of Germany's economic model. For decades, its success relied on high-end manufacturing, highly specialized exporting companies, a skilled workforce, relatively competitive energy costs, and strong international demand. Today, these advantages are being challenged as energy costs remain elevated, demographic aging is increasing labor market pressures, and international competition is intensifying. I am afraid of the emergence of a vicious cycle as weakening competitiveness could discourage investment, slow innovation, and further undermine the country's productive capacity. Moreover, this transformation is taking place at a time when demographic aging is increasing the financial burden of pensions, healthcare, and long-term care.

Germany appears to be gradually losing some of the economic advantages that made it so successful, and without a recovery in competitiveness, what currently looks like an industrial crisis could turn into a lasting crisis of Germany's entire growth model.

*Ifo link (German): https://t.co/dIWUheHNCC
